title: Application of Derivatives: Rates, Increasing Functions, Maxima and Minima
seo_title: Application of Derivatives Class 12 Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 6)
standard_text: Applications of derivatives: rate of change of quantities, increasing/decreasing functions, maxima and minima (first derivative test motivated geometrically and second derivative test given as a provable tool); simple problems that illustrate basic principles and understanding of the subject as well as real life situations (summary of the CBSE syllabus)
meta_desc: Class 12 Application of Derivatives worksheet (NCERT Chapter 6): rate of change, related rates, increasing and decreasing functions, local and absolute maxima and minima and optimisation problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: f′ > 0: increasing; f′ < 0: decreasing; f′ = 0: a critical point.
key_sub: Second derivative test: f″ < 0 gives a maximum, f″ > 0 a minimum.
body_html:
How it works

  • Rate of change: dA/dr, dV/dt and so on. Related rates use the chain rule: dA/dt = (dA/dr)(dr/dt).
  • f is increasing where f′(x) > 0 and decreasing where f′(x) < 0.
  • At a critical point (f′ = 0): f″ < 0 gives a local maximum, f″ > 0 a local minimum.
  • On a closed interval [a, b], the absolute maximum and minimum are among f at the critical points and at a and b.
Example

Find the local maximum of f(x) = x³ − 3x.

f′(x) = 3x² − 3 = 0 at x = ±1

f″(−1) = −6 < 0

Answer: f(−1) = 2

Common mistakes

  • Forgetting to multiply by dr/dt in related rates.
  • Giving the x-value when the question asks for the maximum value.
  • Checking only the critical points on a closed interval.

faq.q: Can a local maximum be smaller than a local minimum?
What if f″ = 0 at a critical point?
faq.a: The second derivative test fails; use the first derivative test.

items.q: The edge of a cube is increasing at 5 cm/s. How fast is the volume increasing when the edge is 12 cm?
items.e: V = x³, so dV/dt = 3x² dx/dt = 3 × 12² × 5 = 2,160 cm³/s.

items.q: The total revenue from selling x units is R(x) = 4x² + 16x + 7 rupees. Find the marginal revenue when x = 6.
items.e: Marginal revenue = dR/dx = 8x + 16; at x = 6 it is ₹64.

items.q: The edge of a cube is increasing at 2 cm/s. How fast is the volume increasing when the edge is 12 cm?
items.e: V = x³, so dV/dt = 3x² dx/dt = 3 × 12² × 2 = 864 cm³/s.

items.q: A rectangle has perimeter 20 cm. What is its largest possible area?
items.e: Area = x(10 − x); it is greatest when x = 5, a square: 25 cm².

items.q: Find the minimum value of x + 4/x for x > 0.
items.e: f′ = 1 − 4/x² = 0 at x = 2; f″ > 0, so the minimum is 2 + 2 = 4.

items.q: Equal squares are cut from the corners of a 18 cm square sheet, and the sides are folded up to make an open box. What side of square gives the largest volume?
items.e: V = x(18 − 2x)²; dV/dx = 0 gives x = 3 (the other root 9 gives no box). 3 cm, volume 432 cm³.

items.q: Two positive numbers have sum 16. Find the largest possible value of their product.
items.e: P = x(16 − x); dP/dx = 16 − 2x = 0 gives x = 8, so the maximum product is 8 × 8 = 64.

items.q: Two positive numbers have sum 24. Find the largest possible value of their product.
items.e: P = x(24 − x); dP/dx = 24 − 2x = 0 gives x = 12, so the maximum product is 12 × 12 = 144.
